title: Synergistic effects of bacterial consortium and thermal energy on sewage treatment
author: Nwajuaku, Agunwamba

steps.title: Construct and cure concrete ponds
steps.instruction: Build three rectangular concrete ponds (ICCP‑A, B, C) using plain cement concrete grade M15 according to IS 456‑2000 with mix ratio 1:2:4 (cement:sand:aggregate), Portland cement 33 grade, natural river sand 4.75 mm, crushed granite aggregate 40 mm, water‑cement ratio 0.40, water absorption 0.20 %, pH 7.7, placed by hand; dimensions: A 1.5 × 0.38 × 0.6 m, B 1.5 × 0.30 × 0.6 m, C 1.5 × 0.25 × 0.6 m; freeboard 0.9 m, wall thickness 0.1016 m. Cure the poured concrete for 28 days at room temperature.

steps.title: Apply primer and thermal paint
steps.instruction: Using a wall brush, coat the interior surfaces of each cured pond with Isonem universal primer diluted 1:7 with water; let dry 4 h. Then apply thermal black paint (ISO 321) in three thin coats, each 1 mm thick, spacing the coats 4 h apart. Allow the painted surface to cure under ambient temperature for a total of 72 h before use.

steps.title: Isolate bacterial strains and select consortium
steps.instruction: Perform a ten‑fold serial dilution of pond water from UNN’s facultative pond, plate 0.1 mL of each dilution onto Nutrient Agar (Titan Biotech) prepared per manufacturer’s instructions using pour‑plate technique, and incubate plates at 37 °C for 24 h to obtain mixed cultures. Record isolated colonies and purify each by repeated sub‑culturing on fresh media to obtain pure cultures (primary isolation as per Zhang et al.). Conduct a bioremediation screening on each isolate by measuring BOD and COD every 24 h for 5 days; select the three most efficient strains (S1, S7, S10). Verify that no zone of inhibition occurs at the intersection of isolates; adopt the three strains as a bacterial consortium.

steps.title: Prepare bacterial inoculum
steps.instruction: Inoculate each consortium strain separately into Trypticase Soy Broth and incubate at 37 °C for 24 h. Centrifuge each culture at 12 000 rpm for 10 min, wash the pellet twice with sterile normal saline, and resuspend in sterile normal saline. Adjust each suspension in nephelometer tubes to 0.5 McFarland standard (optical density 0.1 at 620 nm) with sterile saline. Mix the three adjusted suspensions in equal volumes to obtain a final inoculum concentration of 1 × 10⁸ cells mL⁻¹.

steps.title: Set up evaluation system and run experiments
steps.instruction: Arrange six rectangular concrete ponds: three coated (ICCP‑A, B, C) and three uncoated controls (CA, CB, CC), each duplicated for triplicate runs. Connect a mixing tank (0.18 m³) fed from an overhead tank (4 m³) containing settled sewage; operate the tank at constant head. Add inoculum to the mixing tank at volume fractions of 1.7 %, 3.3 %, and 5.0 % (v/v) for separate experimental runs. After inoculation, allow a 48‑hour acclimation period for bacterial growth. Then let sewage flow gravitationally through a 25‑mm branched pipe into the ICCP ponds. Operate ponds A, B, and C at hydraulic loading rates of 80.92, 62, and 58 m³ d⁻¹ m⁻² respectively, giving a total flow of 120.96 m³ d⁻¹. Perform each experimental condition in triplicate and compare results with the control ponds where no inoculum is added.
